title: Developer Experience Docs Playbook: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, and Support Fixes
author: Avery Chen
body:
Overview

This playbook documents the standard approach for Developer Experience (DevEx) content at Redwood Inference: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, canonical API examples, docs site operating procedures, and the top support issues with canonical fixes. The goal is to make all outward-facing developer-facing documentation consistent, discoverable, and actionable so engineers can onboard quickly and troubleshoot reliably.

Intended audience
- Developer Experience engineers and writers
- SDK owners and API/product engineers
- Developer support and solutions engineers
- On-call engineers who diagnose and fix customer issues

Goals and outcomes
- Canonicalize SDK and Quickstart structure so users complete a task in < 10 minutes for simple flows.
- Provide copy-paste API examples for common languages (Python, JS/Node, curl) and for advanced features (streaming, tool-calls, embeddings).
- Ship a lightweight review and publishing workflow that keeps docs accurate and reduces support load.
- Maintain a prioritized list of top support issues with exact reproduction steps and canonical fixes so support can resolve T1 issues in a single interaction.

Document types and templates (required sections)
All DevEx docs should follow these headings and include the items below:
- Title (short, action-oriented)
- Short intro (1-2 paragraphs describing when to use)
- Prerequisites (account, API keys, SDK versions, environment)
- Step-by-step quickstart (numbered steps with expected output)
- Code snippets (Python, Node, curl minimum; additional languages optional)
- Troubleshooting / common errors (pair symptoms with canonical fixes)
- Related pages / links (internal pages, API reference, release notes)
- Ownership & last updated metadata

Template: Quickstart (required)
1) Install
   - e.g., pip install redwood-sdk==<recommended-version>
2) Configure credentials
   - export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_xxx
3) Minimal request (Python)
   - code sample and expected JSON response snippet
4) Next steps / links to guides and examples

SDK guides: structure and content guidance
- Purpose: Teach idiomatic usage for each language SDK and cover integration patterns (sync, async, streaming, retries, batching).
- Split guidance into: Getting started, Authentication & config, Core primitives (requests, responses, streaming), Advanced patterns (tool calling, structured outputs), Migration notes (breaking changes).
- Versioning: Each SDK guide must include a Supported Versions table with the latest stable, known-bad versions, and the minimum supported version of the SDK and Python/Node runtime. Example:

Supported Versions
| SDK | Latest stable | Minimum supported | Notes |
|-----|---------------|------------------|-------|
| python-redwood | 2.4.1 | 3.8 | streaming GA 2.3+ |

- Code style: prefer short, copy-paste blocks with comments. Keep examples under 30 lines where possible.

Quickstarts & templates library
- One-pagers: 3-5 minute start guides for the top 10 flows (text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking, streaming).
- Sample apps: minimal reference apps (Flask + Redis cache example; Next.js + server-side generation) hosted in internal repo devex/examples.
- Templates: Boilerplate repo templates for common integrations (webhook bots, customer support summarization pipeline, embeddings search). Each template must include: README, minimal infra hint (Dockerfile, terraform snippet), and a telemetry+cost example.

API examples (canonical snippets)
- Languages: Python, Node (fetch/axios), curl. For each code example include: request, expected success response, common error response and diagnosis.
- Streaming example (Python async): provide both the high-level helper and a low-level socket-style reader.
- Function/tool calling: example payloads with schema and canonical parsing.

Example canonical Python snippet (minimal generation):

from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-1x", prompt="Translate to French: 'Hello world'")
print(resp.text)

cURL equivalent:
curl -X POST \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-1x","prompt":"Translate to French: \"Hello world\""}' \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

Docs site operating procedures (publishing & maintenance)
- Authoring workflow
  1. Draft in local markdown or Confluence sandbox; include full code and expected outputs.
  2. Peer review by at least one SDK maintainer and one support engineer.
  3. Add labels and link to related pages.
  4. Final review: product/owner sign-off for breaking changes (e.g., API changes, new endpoints).
  5. Publish and announce on #devex and release-notes channel if user-facing change.
- Review cadence
  - Quarterly reviews for all quickstarts and SDK Guides.
  - Monthly sync between DevEx and Support to refresh the Top Issues list.
- Emergency updates
  - If a production bug impacts an example or guide, DevEx author should push a patch within the current sprint and tag the release notes with the incident ID.

Top support issues and canonical fixes (current prioritized list)
1) 401 / Invalid API key after SDK upgrade
   - Symptom: 401 returned when calling generate() immediately after upgrading SDK to a version that changed auth header name.
   - Root cause: Environment variable not picked up or header name changed from X-API-Key to Authorization: Bearer.
   - Canonical fix: Update credentials per quickstart. Run: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_...; restart service. If using old header, update code to use Authorization: Bearer token.
   - Related doc: SDK auth guide (link).

2) Streaming client disconnects after ~30s
   - Symptom: client receives partial stream then connection closed with ECONNRESET.
   - Root cause: corporate HTTP proxy with aggressive idle timeout or intermediate load balancer not configured for chunked streaming.
   - Canonical fix: Add keepalive/heartbeat headers, increase proxy timeout, or fall back to short-polling > retries example. Include sample Node fetch options: keepalive: true, timeout: 0.

3) Embedding similarity mismatch vs reference
   - Symptom: search results appear unrelated or ranking inconsistent with expectations.
   - Root cause: mismatched vector normalization or using different model/metric than reference.
   - Canonical fix: Confirm model id and vector normalization. Provide script to re-embed dataset and run sanity checks (cosine similarity > 0.75 for identical docs).

4) High token cost from unbounded prompt expansion
   - Symptom: Monthly token invoice spikes after a feature rollout.
   - Root cause: missing prompt length guardrails or server-side loop appending model responses to the prompt.
   - Canonical fix: Add prompt truncation utility, set max_tokens in request, and add alerts when average tokens per request > threshold.

5) Retry storms and rate-limit 429s on bursty traffic
   - Symptom: 429s followed by retry storms causing longer outages.
   - Root cause: client retries too aggressively without jitter/backoff.
   - Canonical fix: Implement exponential backoff with full jitter and capped concurrency. Example policy: initial=200ms, multiplier=2, max=10s, attempts=5.

Ownership, SLAs, and escalation
- DevEx owners: @devex-team (primary), with rotating on-call reviewer from Support.
- SLA for doc fixes: Critical (page-breaking or security): 24h; High (examples broken): 3 business days; Normal: next sprint.
- Escalation: if support cannot resolve with canonical fix, open a triage ticket in the devex-support board and notify the author and SDK owner.

Metrics and observability for docs health
- Track: pageviews, average time on page, copy-paste rates (via snippet telemetry), support ticket references per page.
- Targets: Top 10 quickstarts should have median success time < 10 minutes and support ticket rate < 0.5% of new users.

Appendix: common CLI commands and snippets
- Validate local build:
  make docs-serve && open http://localhost:8000/devex/quickstarts
- Example to run integration test for examples:
  pytest examples/test_sample_app.py -k smoke
